topic: Poliovirus: Live bOPV vs Inactivated IPV Contraindications
entry_criteria: Infant or child presenting for routine poliovirus vaccination (bOPV or IPV)
danger_signs: Severe immunocompromised status (symptomatic HIV, primary immunodeficiency)
Anaphylaxis history to neomycin, streptomycin, or polymyxin B
mandated_actions: Screen immune status prior to oral polio (bOPV) administration
Substitute oral live bOPV with Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV) if severely immunocompromised
Record vaccine formulation administered in child health card
negative_boundaries: 🛑 STRICT CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give live bOPV to severely immunocompromised infants -> High risk of VAPP.
🛑 DO NOT vaccinate with IPV if history of anaphylaxis to streptomycin, neomycin, or polymyxin B.

entry_criteria: Infant presenting for routine Rotavirus vaccine schedule (6 and 10 weeks)
danger_signs: Prior history of intussusception or bowel obstruction
Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) or symptomatic immunodeficiency
Acute severe vomiting, diarrhea, or acute febrile illness
mandated_actions: Screen infant for past intussusception or bowel abnormalities
Confirm immune competence prior to oral live rotavirus vaccine administration
Temporarily defer rotavirus administration during acute gastroenteritis
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give Rotavirus vaccine if infant has prior history of intussusception.
🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give Rotavirus vaccine in infants with SCID or severe immunodeficiency.

topic: BCG: Immunodeficiency & Maternal HIV Exposure Safety
entry_criteria: Newborn or infant eligible for BCG tuberculosis vaccination
danger_signs: Confirmed symptomatic HIV or severe congenital immunodeficiency
Systemic immunosuppressive therapy in infant or late pregnancy
Active systemic illness, generalized lymphadenopathy, or failure to thrive
mandated_actions: Screen maternal HIV status and infant clinical HIV staging prior to BCG
Give BCG at birth to asymptomatic HIV-exposed infants with early virological testing
Withhold BCG in infants with symptomatic HIV until confirmed immune reconstitution on ART
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give BCG if infant has symptomatic HIV or immunodeficiency -> Risk of fatal disseminated BCGitis.
🛑 DO NOT vaccinate with BCG during pregnancy or in infants under 1 year on immunosuppressants.

topic: Measles Live Vaccine: Severe Immunosuppression Safety
entry_criteria: Child eligible for routine Measles/MR vaccine (9 and 15-18 months)
danger_signs: Severe immunosuppression (advanced HIV/AIDS Stage 3-4, leukaemia, lymphoma)
History of severe anaphylactic reaction to neomycin or gelatin
mandated_actions: Screen child for severe immunosuppressive disease or chemotherapy
Administer measles vaccine to HIV-infected children who are NOT severely immunosuppressed
Administer 0.5 mL subcutaneously once clearance confirmed
negative_boundaries: 🛑 ABSOLUTE CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT give live Measles vaccine to severely immunosuppressed individuals (Stage 4 HIV, low CD4%).
🛑 CONTRAINDICATION: DO NOT vaccinate pregnant women or individuals with severe anaphylaxis to neomycin or gelatin.
